light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

clips.text: La primera, y la que más se repite: ¿se puede guardar para el otro día? Mira lo que pasa.
clips.action: he lifts the lid of an old bucket with hardened grey-white lumps inside and shows it to the camera.

clips.d1: close view of a stick pushing into a thick lumpy grey-white paste in a bucket, the paste cracking in chunks
clips.d2: the stick stuck upright in the hardened lumpy paste
clips.text: Esto lo preparé ayer con el cemento adentro. Grumos. Ya no pinta igual, por más que lo revuelvas.
¿Por qué? Porque el cemento empieza a fraguar en cuanto le cae agua. No espera a que tú termines.
clips.action: he taps the bag of white cement with his finger, explaining.

clips.text: Entonces la regla es sencilla: el cemento se mezcla sólo con lo que vas a usar ese día.
clips.action: he puts the lid back on the old bucket and slides it away across the bench.

clips.text: La cal sola, en cambio, sí aguanta. Tapada, con un dedito de agua encima, dura semanas. Por eso separo.
clips.action: he pats the lid of another bucket full of soaked lime paste, satisfied.

clips.text: Segunda pregunta: ¿kilos o botes? Un bote de cal no pesa lo mismo que un bote de cemento.
clips.action: he holds up a clear plastic jug of lime powder next to a kitchen scale, comparing.

clips.text: La cal es mucho más liviana. Si mides la cal en kilos y el cemento en jarras, te sale otra mezcla.
clips.action: he puts the jug on the scale, reads it, then puts a same jug of cement on the scale.

clips.text: Por eso todo en jarras, con la misma jarra. Cuatro de cal, una de cemento. Así no te equivocas nunca.
clips.action: he taps the same jug twice, nodding.

clips.text: Cuarta pregunta: ¿cuánto dura? No te voy a inventar un número. Depende de la lluvia, del sol, y de cómo la pongas.
clips.action: he sits on a stool by the bench and holds up four fingers, thinking.

clips.text: Lo bueno es que cuando se gasta no hay que raspar nada: se moja y se le pasa otra mano encima, y queda como nueva.
clips.action: he stands up from the stool and pats the bucket of lime, smiling.

clips.d1: close view of a kitchen scale on a workbench with a jug of white powder on it, the display blank
clips.d2: the same jug being lifted off the scale by a hand
